summary: John's 1st cousin 7x removed; early coal operator ruined by the trade.
bio:
Daniel Davenport (1797-1840) 'became seriously involved in the coal trade' and lost most of his estate; Wright, who sat on the same school bench, says these troubles 'undoubtedly' caused his early death.

Giles & Franklin say Daniel was born at Plymouth on 7 or 9 March 1796 or 1797, died on 3 Sep 1840, and married Mary Nesbitt (b. Plymouth 3 Mar 1803) on 12 Mar 1820. Their children were Charles (b. 27 May 1821), George (4 Jan 1823 - 27 Jun 1906, m. Emily Ingham), Chester (b. 7 Feb 1825, d. Dec 1855), Esther (b. 14 May 1827, m. William Garrahan), Harriet (b. 2 Apr 1830), James (b. 3 May 1831) and Hendrick Wright Davenport (b. 6 Dec 1834, d. Culbertson, Neb., 9 Jul 1916) ([R4-S1]). The youngest was evidently named for H. B. Wright, who sat on the same school bench as Daniel. In 1823 Daniel and John Lamoreaux built a sawmill on Bidlack's Creek ([R4-S2]).
sources: [R4-S1] Giles & Franklin, Thomas Davenport ... and his Descendants (1962), pp.320-321 (secondary) https://archive.org/details/thomasdavenportp00gile
[R4-S2] H. C. Bradsby, History of Luzerne County (1893), p.589 (secondary) https://archive.org/details/historyofluzerne00brad
